title: Ruta del Jefe Returns to Arizona’s Sky Islands in April 2027
content:
Ruta del Jefe Returns to Arizona’s Sky Islands in April 2027. This is more than just a gravel ride; it is five cycling routes, four days of community, and a $100,000 fundraising goal that bring a distinctive approach to adventure cycling in the Arizona-Sonora Borderlands.

Ruta del Jefe 2027

Ruta del Jefe returns to the rugged landscapes of southern Arizona April 1–4, 2027, inviting cyclists to explore the Sky Islands through a four-day gathering that combines challenging gravel and adventure riding with education, community, and collective impact.

Held in Patagonia, Arizona, Ruta del Jefe offers five Saturday routes ranging from approximately 30 to 78 miles, with options spanning approachable gravel rides to demanding backcountry adventures featuring thousands of feet of climbing.

But the experience extends well beyond the routes.

Founded by adventure cyclist and route developer Sarah Swallow, Ruta del Jefe brings riders together to learn about the people, cultures, ecosystems, and challenges that shape the Arizona-Sonora Borderlands.

“Adventure cycling gives us an incredible opportunity to connect with the landscapes we travel through,” says Swallow. “Ruta del Jefe asks what happens when we take that connection further, when we get curious about the people who live there, learn about the challenges facing the region, and find ways to contribute.”

Five Routes Through the Sky Islands

The 2027 event features five supported ride options:

  • El Jefe: 78 miles, approximately 6,000 feet of climbing. A challenging adventure route.
  • Sombra: 68 miles, approximately 4,447 feet of climbing. A demanding gravel-plus experience.
  • Cinco: 55 miles, approximately 4,969 feet of climbing. A rugged adventure route.
  • O:Shad: 45 miles, approximately 3,289 feet of climbing. A shorter gravel-plus option.
  • Adela: 30 miles, approximately 1,859 feet of climbing. A more approachable gravel route.

Participants will encounter the region’s characteristic mix of remote roads, rugged mountains, grasslands, and expansive Borderlands scenery.

Additional community rides, workshops, and educational activities take place throughout the four-day gathering.

Riding With Purpose

Beyond Saturday’s main rides, Ruta del Jefe includes presentations and workshops led by organizations working across the Arizona-Sonora Borderlands.

The event’s 2027 fundraising goal is $100,000, benefiting six organizations: Borderlands Restoration Network, Kino Border Initiative, San Xavier Cooperative Farm, La Tierra del Jaguar, Sierra Club Borderlands Program, and Sky Island Alliance.

The organizations’ work spans ecological restoration, wildlife conservation, Indigenous food sovereignty, migrant dignity, and environmental advocacy.

Participants are encouraged not only to raise funds but also to engage directly with the organizations and learn about their work.

A Different Kind of Cycling Gathering

Hosted at Borderlands Restoration Network’s Native Plant Nursery and Seed Lab, Ruta del Jefe centers community rather than competition.

The event combines camping, shared meals, supported riding, educational programming, cultural experiences, and live music in an immersive four-day format.

Registration is now open, with general admission priced at $595 and limited Access Fund tickets available for $345. Fully funded scholarships also support participation.

Ruta del Jefe 2027
April 1–4 | Patagonia, Arizona
